Princess Patricia, the daughter of the Governor Genral at the time, the Duke of Connaught, was Colonel-in-Chief of the eponymous Canadian Infantry regiment and held that appointment until her death. The regiment named for her was privately raised by Andrew Hamilton Gault, of Montreal, at his own expense; for service in the First World War and was the last privately raised regiment in the British Empire. The regiment also participated in the Second World War, the Korean War and the War in Afghanistan, as well as in numerous NATO operations and United Nations peacekeeping missions in Israel, Golan, Egypt, Lebanon, Kuwait, Iraq, Congo, Vietnam, Central America, Angola, Somalia, Rwanda, Croatia, and Bosnia. The regiment has received 39 battle honours, three Commander-in-Chief Unit Commendations and the United States Presidential Unit Citation. Source.
